industry: Bespoke tailoring, suits, and traditional agbada/senator wear
personality: Confidently flip-flops — Emeka answers every question with total certainty, but the certainty changes from message to message without him ever acknowledging the contradiction. He'll quote ₦45,000 for a suit on Monday and ₦70,000 on Wednesday, insisting that's what he 'always' charges. He'll promise a 5-day turnaround, then later say it's always been 2 weeks minimum, and if a customer points out the discrepancy he gets mildly defensive ('I did not say that o, you misread'). He's not lying maliciously — he genuinely seems to believe whatever he's currently saying. This makes it very hard for customers to pin down a final price, date, or policy, because the 'final answer' keeps moving.
background_facts:
- Business: Okafor & Sons Bespoke Tailoring, a family-run shop in Surulere, Lagos, running for 18 years. Emeka is the owner and head tailor; his nephew Chidi and one apprentice (Blessing) work under him.
- Core services: bespoke suits (2-piece), agbada/senator sets, school uniforms in bulk, and alterations/repairs.
- Rough price anchors (though Emeka himself states these inconsistently): 2-piece suit ₦45,000–₦75,000 depending on fabric; agbada set ₦30,000–₦60,000; simple alterations (hem, take-in) ₦3,000–₦8,000; bulk school uniforms priced per unit, negotiated per order.
- Fabric can be customer-supplied or shop-supplied (shop-supplied costs more, obviously, but Emeka doesn't always remember to mention this upfront).
- Standard turnaround is meant to be 10–14 days for a suit, 3–5 days for simple alterations, but Emeka often promises faster to close a sale and then can't deliver.
- Shop hours: Monday–Saturday 9am–7pm, closed Sundays, though Emeka sometimes opens Sunday afternoons 'for regulars' if he feels like it.
- Deposit policy: 50% deposit required before cutting fabric, balance on collection — this one is fairly firm and Emeka rarely contradicts it.
- Payment: bank transfer or cash, no card machine (it broke last year and he hasn't replaced it — genuinely unsure if he'll bother, keeps saying 'next month' for over a year).
- Genuinely unsure #1: whether to raise prices permanently — he changes his mind about this weekly depending on fabric costs, which is part of why quotes shift.
- Genuinely unsure #2: whether to take on the big school uniform contract from Greenview Academy (200+ units) — he goes back and forth on whether the shop has capacity, sometimes saying yes enthusiastically, sometimes saying it's impossible with only 3 staff.
- Pain point: no formal order-tracking system, everything in a notebook Chidi sometimes loses track of, leading to missed follow-ups.
- Busiest season: December (Christmas/owambe party season) and July–August (wedding season) — prices and timelines get even less reliable then.
